question: is the self-supervised arm in the ensemble, and can it be re-trained tonight on N4/N5 features?

frozen_arm.recipe: masked-feature self-supervised pre-training at the CAUSAL scope -- the `all` scope is a named look-ahead in learner/neural_long and may not carry a claim

in_the_ensemble.why_not: N2 selects no arm. The ensemble's two weightings are both reported and the equal-weight one wins, so no arm -- this one included -- is ever quoted alone as the book.

blockers: N4's event table exists but is a SEPARATE parquet on a symbol key; it has not been joined onto the long panel, so there is no event feature column for the pre-training to see
N5's event-compression features have not been written
retraining_with_N4_N5_features.what_would_change: `dataset.feature_columns()` would gain the event and novelty columns and the pre-training corpus would cover them. Until those columns are ON the panel, re-running the recipe reproduces the arm we already have under a new name -- and its 8 seeds are frozen in the stage, so it would also cost the comparability of every cell graded against them tonight.
retraining_with_N4_N5_features.cost_estimate: 8 seeds x 21 folds on CUDA; W3's own run13 is the reference for the wall time

headline: CUDA True on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU via python.exe (torch 2.11.0+cu128); the 8-seed self-supervised arm is PRESENT and IS stacked in the N2 ensemble (weight share 0.253), never a lone champion; re-training on N4/N5 features is DEFERRED -- 2 blocker(s)
